newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down 3.92 percent.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down 3.92 percent.

text.p: Thai stocks fell sharply on Friday and closed nearly four percent lower as foreign investors continued to sell during the afternoon session, traders said.

Late buying pared heavier losses earlier in the session and the SET Index ended down 32.14 points at 788.04 .The SET 50 ended down 2.95 points, or 4.81 percent, to 58.44 points. Turnover was a brisk 7.69 billion baht.

European sell orders at around 0850 GMT intensified earlier foreign selling pressure, taking the SET to an intraday low of 782.07 at approximately 0920 GMT, before last minute bargain-hunting helped boost the market, traders said.
"There was concern from foreigners on the currency today, local buyers were pretty much sidelined watching the developments," said a senior trader at Dynamic Eastern.

After touching 26 baht per dollar on Thursday, the Thai currency was weaker early in offshore markets against the dollar on Friday, causing foreigners to dump Thai equities throughout the day, traders said.
Foreign sentiment on the baht and stocks was hurt by trade data released on Thursday, analysts said.

The figures showed Thailand posted a balance of payments deficit of 19.2 billion baht in December, a $900 million decline in foreign reserves last month, and a steady decline in manufacturing output growth.
"The interesting thing is foreigners offloaded major stocks across the board even defensive stocks in energy and building materials. It indicates sentiment was very bad," said a senior Thai analyst.
"The pressure on the baht will certainly keep interest rates high in the immediate future, meaning lower growth and higher costs," he said.
The bank sector lost 5.72 percent, communications 5.47 percent, finance 5.92 percent, and energy 4.47 percent.
Bangkok Bank lost 10 baht to 176, Thai Farmers Bank fell nine to 118, and Siam Commercial Bank shed eight to 161.
Finance One retreated three baht to 34.25, Securities One fell limit down 8.50 baht to 77, and PTTEP lost 16 to 370.
